'''''Solidago azorica''''' is a species of [[goldenrod]] in the family [[Asteraceae]], endemic to the [[Azores]], [[Portugal]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Solidago azorica Hochst. |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/4Y769 |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref> It is closely related to ''[[Solidago sempervirens]]'', native to eastern North America, but in addition to the morphological differences there is a clear genetic separation between the two species.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schaefer |first1=Hanno |title=On the origin and systematic position of the Azorean goldenrod, Solidago azorica (Asteraceae) |journal=Phytotaxa |date=2015-05-29 |volume=210 |issue=1 |pages=47 |doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.210.1.5 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/278025983 |access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref> This species is thought to have evolved from its American relative from a natural introduction made well before human occupation on the islands.<ref name="siaram">{{cite web |title=Solidago sempervirens L. |url=http://siaram.azores.gov.pt/flora/flora-vascular/cubres/flora-vascular-cubres.pdf |website=siaram.azores.gov.pt |access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref>

==Description==
Stems are up to {{convert|60|cm|abbr=on}} long; it has numerous leaves, which are apicular and slightly thick; it produces a large number of small yellow flowers.<ref name="siaram" />

==Distribution==
It is found in coastal cliffs, lava flows and sand or stone deposits in rough terrain. It occurs dispersed in coastal meadows dominated by ''[[Festuca petraea]]'', as well as in heavily exposed habitats, along paths and along stone walls. Up to about {{convert|500|m|abbr=on}} altitude ({{convert|900|m|abbr=on}} in [[Flores Island (Azores)|Flores]]). It is present in all of the nine Azorean islands.<ref>{{cite web |title=Euphorbia azorica Seub. |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/1Euphorbia+azorica |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=24 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Euphorbia azorica Hochst. |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3CMY9 |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=24 March 2021}}</ref><ref name="siaram" />
